spec.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
spec.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is an irreducible L_K-module. This holds including λ=0 and p=2 and without any algebraic-closure assumption on K.

propositions.statement: Let A be a commutative semiring, S a submonoid of A, C0 a commutative A-algebra which is a localization of A at S, B an additive commutative monoid and A-module, B1 an additive commutative monoid with A- and C0-module structures forming a scalar tower, and f:B→B1 an A-linear map. Then IsLocalizedModule(S,f) if and only if IsBaseChange(C0,f). The first predicate says: each s∈S acts invertibly on B1; for each z∈B1 there exist b∈B and s∈S with s z=f(b); and f(b)=f(b') implies s b=s b' for some s∈S. The second predicate says that the canonical C0-linear tensor map C0⊗_A B→B1, c⊗b↦c f(b), is bijective (and thus a linear isomorphism).

propositions.statement: n=λ+1>0, |I|=n, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V, so dim_C V=n. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Moreover y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher lowering powers vanish. On the basis: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤λ; ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ; ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} when r≤i and zero when r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix entries are integers.

μ:M_R→V is injective and identifies M_R with an R-submodule of V which is free of rank n, spans V over C, and is preserved by every X_r and Y_r (r≥0). For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and P0=E_{λλ}, X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}, P0 Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0 Y_{λ−j}. Consequently every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The operators x,y,h preserve M and hence act on V_K and the localized module.

All modules J_i (i∈I) equal J. The R-module J⊂C is nonzero and finitely generated, and μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I} J e_i internally in V. The multiplication map Q⊗_R J→QJ⊂C, q⊗c↦qc, is injective and surjective onto QJ. With r=dim_Q(Q⊗_R J), r is finite and dim_Q(Q⊗_R M_R)=n=n r; hence r=1 and dim_Q QJ=1.

binders.type: natural number defined here as dim_Q(Q⊗_R J)

propositions.statement: There exists b∈J with b≠0 such that J=Rb and μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I} R(b e_i). The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of μ(M_R), equivalently its unique μ-preimage is an R-basis of M_R.

There is a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of V_K of cardinality n=λ+1>0 with xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i, all integer coefficients mapped to K. The natural maps give M⊗_Z K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K. For 0≤r≤λ, the induced divided powers are X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r, where r! is nonzero in K. For all i,j∈I, writing P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K, the K-linear operator T_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K satisfies T_ij β_k=β_i if k=j and zero otherwise. Every coefficient inverse in this formula exists in K. Therefore every K-subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under all T_ij.

locals.declaration: Use arbitrary t≥0 for the h induction step and arbitrary t≥1 for the x induction step; the t=1 base is separately checked.
Fix arbitrary i∈I when proving the indexed formulas.

argument.text: H001 gives n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We first prove the commutator formulas for all nonnegative powers. For h, the case t=0 is hv=λv from H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v. Using [h,y]=−2y from H002, h y^{t+1}v=y h y^t v−2y^{t+1}v=(λ−2(t+1))y^{t+1}v. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction proves the h formula for every t≥0. For x, the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=λv by H002 and H003. For t≥1 temporarily assume L2: xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. Discharging L2 proves the step, and induction gives the x formula for all t≥1. These identities are F001.

produces.statement: For every integer z1≥0, hy^z1 v=(λ−2z1)y^z1 v; for z1≥1, xy^z1 v=z1(λ−z1+1)y^{z1−1}v.

argument.text: For i∈I, iterating F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the product is 1 and this is v. All factors for i>0 are positive integers, and v≠0 by H003, so every e_i is nonzero over C. By F001, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i; these eigenvalues are distinct over C. To check independence, fix arbitrary coefficients c=(c_i)_{i∈I} and temporarily assume L3: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id) to this relation. It yields c_j∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0. The product, including an empty product, is nonzero, and e_j≠0, hence c_j=0. Discharge L3 to obtain independence. H002 gives dim_C V=n, and there are n independent e_i, so they form a complex basis. This proves F002.

produces.statement: The family (e_z1)_{z1∈I} is a complex basis of V; each e_z1 is nonzero, he_z1=(λ−2z1)e_z1, and dim_C V=n.

argument.text: F001 specialized to exponent λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if it is nonzero. Temporarily assume L4 that it is nonzero. Expanding it in the basis F002, the equality h y^{λ+1}v=(−λ−2)y^{λ+1}v forces every coefficient to vanish: for i∈I, (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i) is a nonzero complex scalar. This is a contradiction, so discharge L4 to conclude y^{λ+1}v=0. Applying further y powers gives all higher vanishing. F001 divided by i!, together with this termination and xv=0 from H003, gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. This proves F003.

produces.statement: y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers vanish. For z1∈I, xe_0=0 and xe_z1=(λ−z1+1)e_{z1−1} if z1≥1; ye_z1=(z1+1)e_{z1+1} if z1<λ and ye_λ=0; he_z1=(λ−2z1)e_z1.

argument.text: Iterate the displayed x,y matrices in F003 and divide by r!. For each natural r and i∈I with r≤i, x^r e_i/r!=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r}. If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed by x. For i+r≤λ, y^r e_i/r!=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r}; otherwise it passes the last vector and is zero. For r=0 the empty products are 1. These are precisely X_r,Y_r by definition. The displayed binomial coefficients, with nonnegative integer upper argument at least r, are integers. Together with F001–F003 this is every assertion of the asserted conclusion.

argument.text: H004 gives an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. By N001, dim_C V=n and |I|=n. Equality of the cardinalities of finite bases permits reindexing the given lattice basis by I. Thus there exists a family m=(m_i)_{i∈I} which is simultaneously a Z-basis of M and a complex basis of V. This is F001.

produces.statement: There exists a family z1:I→M which is a Z-basis of M and whose image in V is a complex basis.

argument.text: Choose such a family m using F001. Since R is a commutative Z-algebra, M001 with A=Z, B=M, C0=R and d=m gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Its image under μ is the family m_i in V. A relation in its kernel is a finite R-linear relation among the complex-independent m_i, so all coefficients are zero. Thus μ is injective; the image is free of rank n and spans V over C. By H004, all X_r,Y_r preserve M, so their scalar extensions preserve M_R and μ intertwines them. Also x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=xy−yx preserves M because H002 gives [x,y]=h. This proves h-stability. Record F002: μ is injective with the claimed free, spanning and stability properties.

produces.statement: μ is injective; μ(M_R) is free of rank n over R and spans V over C; every X_z1 and Y_z1 preserves it. The operators x,y,h preserve M and extend to M_R and V_K.

argument.text: For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

argument.text: Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

produces.statement: J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C, every J_i equals J, and μ(M_R)=⊕_{aidx∈I}J e_aidx. There are R-linear coordinate maps coord_aidx:M_R→J and insertion maps ins_aidx:J→M_R. For u0∈M_R, μ(u0)=∑_{aidx∈I}coord_aidx(u0)e_aidx; for c0∈J, μ(ins_aidx(c0))=c0 e_aidx. The composite coord_aidx∘ins_bidx is zero when aidx≠bidx and the identity when aidx=bidx, and ∑_{aidx∈I}ins_aidx∘coord_aidx=Id.

argument.text: Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.

produces.statement: Q is a localization of R at S_R; f:J→QJ is the R-linear inclusion, its target has compatible R- and Q-module structures, and it satisfies IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f). QJ is finite-dimensional over Q.

argument.text: Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. In fraction language a zero image forces a zero numerator, since J⊂C is torsion-free. Define T_Q=Q⊗_R J and r=dim_Q T_Q. The isomorphism and F002 show this dimension is finite. Record F003.

produces.statement: Multiplication T_Q=Q⊗_R J→QJ⊂C is a Q-linear isomorphism onto QJ and injective into C. T_Q is finite-dimensional, with dimension r.

argument.text: Set A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R. Instantiate the coordinate and insertion maps of F001, denoting them α_i and τ_i. Their scalar extensions give a Q-linear map A_Q→(T_Q)^I sending q⊗u to (q⊗α_i(u))_{i∈I}. Its inverse sends a tuple (z_i) to ∑_{i∈I}(1⊗τ_i)(z_i); here 1⊗τ_i denotes the tensor map q⊗c↦q⊗τ_i(c). These maps are well-defined by R-balancing. The equalities α_iτ_j=δ_ij Id and ∑τ_iα_i=Id in F001 verify the two composite identities, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus A_Q≅(T_Q)^I as Q-vector spaces. This proves F004.

produces.statement: A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R is Q-linearly isomorphic to the finite product (T_Q)^I by the coordinate tensor map and the sum of insertion tensor maps.

argument.text: N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R with n elements. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R and C0=Q to this basis: its scalar extension is a Q-basis of A_Q with n elements, so dim_Q A_Q=n. Apply M003 with A=Q, index type I and constant module family T_Q. The field Q satisfies the strong rank condition by finite-dimensional linear algebra; I is finite with n elements by N001. By F003 each T_Q is finite-dimensional, hence free and finitely generated over Q. M003 gives dim_Q((T_Q)^I)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. F004 therefore gives n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, cancellation in the natural numbers yields r=1. F003 now gives dim_Q QJ=1, while F001 gives the finite generation, nonzero property and decomposition. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

argument.text: Choose 0≠a∈J using N003. N003 identifies Q⊗_R J with the one-dimensional subspace QJ⊂C. Since a≠0, a is a Q-basis of that line. Take finite generators of J, discard any zero generators, and use J≠0 to see the remaining list is nonempty. Every remaining generator is a nonzero rational multiple of a. Therefore there exist k≥1 and q_1,…,q_k∈Q\{0} such that J is generated over R by q_1a,…,q_ka. This is F001.

produces.statement: There exist z1≥1 and a family z2 indexed by {1,…,z1} of nonzero rational numbers such that J=∑_{j=1}^z1 R(z2_j a).

argument.text: Choose k,q as in F001. For each 1≤j≤k, write q_j as a ratio of nonzero integers, remove the maximal powers of the prime p from numerator and denominator, and define ν_j to be the difference of these two exponents. Then q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a rational whose numerator and denominator are both prime to p. Such u_j and its reciprocal belong to R, so u_j is a unit. This construction also covers negative ν_j. Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j and b=p^ν a. The minimum exists and is attained because k≥1 and the list is finite. All q_j a belong to Rb, since q_j a=p^{ν_j−ν}u_j b and ν_j−ν≥0. Also b≠0, since p is prime by H001 and a≠0. Record F002, including the existence of a minimizing index.

produces.statement: b=p^ν a≠0, every q_z1 a belongs to Rb, each u_z1 is a unit of R with q_z1=p^{ν_z1}u_z1, and there exists z2∈{1,…,k} with ν_{z2}=ν.

argument.text: Choose a minimizing index j0 from F002. Then q_{j0}a=u_{j0}b, and u_{j0} is an R-unit. Since q_{j0}a is a generator of J by F001, b=u_{j0}^{−1}q_{j0}a belongs to J and Rb⊆J. The reverse inclusion follows from F001 and the inclusion of every generator in Rb from F002. Thus J=Rb with b∈J nonzero. This is F003.

Substitute F003 in the direct decomposition of N003 to obtain μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}R(b e_i). The vectors b e_i are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex-independent by N001. They span by the displayed decomposition, so are an R-basis. Since μ is injective by N002, their unique preimages form an R-basis of M_R. Existentially quantify b to prove the asserted conclusion. In particular no rank-one claim has been inferred from containment in C alone.

argument.text: H001 implies that every integer denominator prime to p maps to a nonzero element of K. Define ρ:R→K by ρ(a/b)=a_K b_K^{−1}. Cross multiplication makes this well-defined and a ring homomorphism extending Z→K. There is also the injective prime-field map F_p→K. Define Φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by Φ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c; its inverse is (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c. Both formulas respect the tensor relations (the R-action on K is through ρ), and the composites are identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Next define the map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K by u⊗c↦(u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends a residue tensor (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: replacing u by u+pt changes this by pt⊗c=t⊗pc=0. It is balanced over F_p, and its R-balancing is justified by R/pR≅F_p, explicitly a/b mod p↦a_p b_p^{-1}; the kernel is pR and every residue is obtained from an integer. These maps are inverse on generators. All maps commute with operators induced from M or M_R, by their formulas. Such x,y,h and divided powers exist by N002. This proves the natural identifications in F001.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K is the extension of Z→K, and there are natural K-linear operator-compatible isomorphisms V_K=M⊗_Z K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K. The first sends z1⊗z2 to (1⊗z1)⊗z2 and has inverse (z3⊗z1)⊗z2↦z1⊗ρ(z3)z2; the second sends z4⊗z2 to its residue tensor and its inverse is given by any representative z4.

argument.text: Choose b as in N004. For each i∈I define m_i to be the unique μ-preimage of b e_i; N002 gives injectivity and N004 gives membership and the R-basis property of this family in M_R. Define β_i=Φ^{-1}(m_i⊗1)∈V_K. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R, C0=K, the algebra structure ρ and the R-basis (m_i). It gives the K-basis (1⊗m_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The factor-switching isomorphism c⊗u↦u⊗c (with inverse u⊗c↦c⊗u), followed by Φ^{-1}, gives the K-basis β. It has |I|=n=λ+1>0 elements by N001. Because μ intertwines the divided powers, and b is a common complex scalar, the matrices on m_i are exactly those on e_i from N001. F001 carries these matrices to V_K with every integer entry mapped into K. Thus xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The divided-power matrices also descend: X_r^K β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_{i−r} for r≤i, zero for r>i, and Y_r^K β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ, zero otherwise. Here X_r^K,Y_r^K denote the operators induced from X_r,Y_r on M_R. Record F002.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V_K indexed by I, with n=λ+1>0 elements and with the x,y,h matrices and all induced divided-power matrices stated in S002. Explicitly for z1∈I: xβ_0=0, xβ_z1=(λ−z1+1)β_{z1−1} (z1≥1), yβ_z1=(z1+1)β_{z1+1} (z1<λ), yβ_λ=0, hβ_z1=(λ−2z1)β_z1; X_z2^Kβ_z1=binom(λ−z1+z2,z2)β_{z1−z2} (z2≤z1) and zero otherwise; Y_z2^Kβ_z1=binom(z1+z2,z2)β_{z1+z2} (z1+z2≤λ) and zero otherwise, for every natural z2.

argument.text: N002 gives, inside the localized lattice, E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}, with P0=Y_λX_λ, and says all these factors preserve it. In the basis (b e_i), E_ij has a single entry 1 in position (i,j), the same as in (e_i). Scalar extension through F001 therefore carries the equality to the operator T_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)^{-1})X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K on β, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K. It satisfies T_ijβ_k=β_i for k=j and 0 for k≠j. Since binom(λ,j) is a unit of R by N002, its image is a unit of K (ρ sends its inverse to an inverse). Also for 0≤r≤λ<p, no factor of r! is divisible by p by H001, so r! maps to a nonzero element of K. The equalities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold over C by definition, hence on M_R by injectivity of μ, and after scalar extension. Consequently X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. This proves F003.

produces.statement: For every z1,z2,z3∈I, T_{z1,z2}=binom(λ,z2)_K^{-1}X_{λ−z1}^K P_K Y_{λ−z2}^K, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K, and T_{z1,z2}β_z3=β_z1 if z3=z2 and zero otherwise. All these binomial coefficient inverses exist in K. For every natural z4 with 0≤z4≤λ, z4!_K≠0 and X_z4^K=(z4!_K)^{-1}x^z4, Y_z4^K=(z4!_K)^{-1}y^z4.

argument.text: Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x and y. Induction on the power shows it is invariant under x^r and y^r for every natural r. Because W is K-linear it is stable under scalar multiples and compositions of its preserving operators. F003 expresses all X_r^K,Y_r^K for r≤λ as scalar multiples of these powers, and T_ij as a scalar times a composition of these operators, since λ−i,λ,λ−j are all in [0,λ]. Therefore W is invariant under every T_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with F001–F003, existentially quantify the compatible basis β to obtain the asserted conclusion.

argument.text: Choose a basis β and the compatible matrix operators guaranteed by N005. This basis has n=λ+1>0 elements, so dim_K V_K=n>0 and V_K≠0; record this as F001. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is x,y-invariant, and N005 says it is invariant under every T_ij. By classical cases, either W={0}, which is already one required alternative, or temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. Under L1,L2, a nonzero vector in W has a unique expansion in the basis β; at least one coefficient is nonzero, since a vector with every coefficient zero is zero. Thus there exist w∈W, a coefficient family c:I→K, and j∈I with w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i≠0 and c_j≠0. This is F002 under L1,L2.

produces.statement: There exist z1∈W, z2:I→K, and z3∈I such that z1=∑_{i∈I}z2_iβ_i≠0 and z2_z3≠0; W is invariant under every T_ij.

argument.text: Choose w,c,j as in F002. For every i∈I, linearity and the matrix-unit action in N005 give T_ij w=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiply by c_j^{-1} to get β_i∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine this result with the W={0} case to obtain W={0} or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 to get the implication for this arbitrary W, then universally quantify W. This gives F003 with no remaining local assumptions.

produces.statement: For every K-linear subspace z1 of V_K, if z1 is invariant under x,y,h, then z1={0} or z1=V_K.

argument.text: F001 proves nonzero dimension and F003 proves exactly the required subspace assertion. L_K is spanned over K by the three induced generators x,y,h, so a K-linear subspace is L_K-invariant exactly when it is invariant under those three operators. Thus these assertions are irreducibility of V(K) as an L(K)-module. The original H001 allows λ=0: then I={0}, every relevant factorial and binomial coefficient is 1, and N005 gives the same one-dimensional conclusion. If p=2 the allowed λ are 0 and 1; N005's matrix-unit argument still applies, with no use of distinct h-eigenvalues in K. Nothing used algebraic closure of K. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.
